title: Falling in Love
hook: Valerie wears a new ring after three weeks, and certainty arrives before knowledge.
counterintuition: Romantic intensity can be true and still too thin for marriage. Its power is the problem: it feels like destiny before ordinary sight returns.
tryThisNow: Write one sentence that separates feeling from choosing: "The high may fade, so today I will love by ____." Fill the blank with one visible act.
keyTakeaway: The in-love high can open the door, but lasting love begins when open-eyed spouses choose disciplined care after the feeling stops carrying them.

breakdown.fastRead:
Valerie arrives after dinner with a ring and a story only three weeks old. For years, love had not lasted. Now Christophe feels like the answer, and engagement feels like proof that the search is over.

The ring may be real while the judgment is not yet ready. The in-love high makes virtues glow and warnings shrink. It gives the heart speed before the mind has much evidence.

Early romance is not fake. It is also not enough. Lasting love starts when euphoria fades and a spouse begins to choose care with open eyes.
breakdown.deepRead:
Romantic obsession works by narrowing attention. The loved person seems lit from within. Small faults seem easy to absorb. A warning that would slow a friend can look like proof that outsiders do not understand.

Jaspreet draws "Dorothy Tennov" and "limerence" on a whiteboard before a couples class. The room came for comfort, not a calendar. Yet the words two years change the mood. Romantic obsession has an average span. It rises without much choice, and it can fall without a moral failure.

That helps couples read the drop with less panic. When the high fades, the spouse is not a fraud and the marriage is not exposed as empty. Ordinary sight has returned. Now habits, words, time, repair, and service have to carry what chemistry once carried for free.

The feeling is real, but it is not a maintenance plan. Real love adds will to warmth. It asks what the other person needs for security and growth after the thrill no longer supplies the effort.

After euphoria, the fork is often misread. One path says endure a cold marriage. Another says leave and hunt for the high again. Mature love names a third path: choose the good of the spouse, then practice the love that fills the tank.
breakdown.fullRead:
Etienne's mother notices what his romance refuses to weigh. Bonnie has spent five years in psychiatric care, and Etienne hears the warning as an attack. At the kitchen table, his mother does not deny his affection. She asks him to bring the fact into the light before the wedding plan grows harder to question.

Five years of care does not make Bonnie unworthy of love. That would be the crude reading. The sharper point is about Etienne's judgment. Euphoria can turn concern into disloyalty and make caution feel small-hearted. Real love needs more courage than that. It can honor a person and still ask sober questions.

Dorothy Tennov's frame helps because it lowers the drama around the change. Limerence is a name for the state that feels bigger than choice. It can make the future seem settled while knowledge is still thin. If romantic obsession often averages about two years, then its fading should not be treated as proof that love died.

Rocco meets that fact on an ordinary Thursday, not in a crisis. The apartment is quiet. Pascal is tired. Nothing terrible has happened, but the old rush is gone. Rocco can read the quiet as failure, or he can notice that the automatic fuel has run low.

Pascal needs something better than being chased as a feeling. A full emotional tank gives a spouse safety. Safety frees energy for growth, work, faith, friendship, and repair. Love does not merely keep two people sentimental. It gives them ground under their feet.

Real love begins when the loved person can be seen clearly and still served freely. That is why choice and discipline do not make love less genuine. They make love less dependent on mood. A spouse who acts for the other's good after the thrill fades is not faking love. That spouse is giving love a body.

Romance still has a place. It can open the door, soften fear, and help two people imagine a shared life. The limit is that romance is poor at chores, apologies, budgets, illness, and boredom. It arrives like weather. A marriage needs practices that can be repeated when the weather changes.

Open-eyed love does not excuse harm or erase hard facts. Some relationships need safety, counsel, or distance before any practice can help. The point is not to stay at any cost. The point is to stop using the first high as the ruler for every later day. When the high wears off, love has not lost its only language. It has reached the hour when language must become chosen speech.

examples.title: Valerie Brings the Ring

planSpec.audience: couples moving fast after a romantic surge
planSpec.stakes: slow certainty enough for knowledge to catch up

examples.scenario: Valerie says, "We're engaged," before her coat is off in the counseling-office lobby. The ring is new, the relationship is three weeks old, and years without success make the announcement feel like rescue. Before the intake form is signed, she must tell the counselor what she actually knows about Christophe beyond the glow of engagement.
examples.whatToDo: Valerie slows the story to evidence: what she has seen under stress, what friends have noticed, and which hopes are being supplied by the rush.
examples.whyItMatters: Premature certainty can feel holy when loneliness ends. The pause respects the feeling while refusing to let three weeks do the work of knowledge.

examples.title: Jaspreet Tests the Calendar

planSpec.audience: couples expecting intensity to sustain effort
planSpec.stakes: turn a time limit into preparation rather than panic
planSpec.requiredBeat: Dorothy Tennov's limerence research makes romantic obsession time-limited

examples.scenario: Jaspreet writes "Dorothy Tennov: limerence, two years" on the premarital classroom whiteboard. Couples came in holding romantic obsession as proof that effort will stay easy. Before the first worksheet is handed out, she has to say why an average span is not a sentence against marriage but a warning against using intensity as fuel.
examples.whatToDo: Jaspreet asks each couple to write one action they will choose after the thrill no longer makes the action feel effortless.
examples.whyItMatters: Dorothy Tennov's calendar lowers panic. A time-limited high can be honored without expecting it to run the whole marriage.

examples.title: Etienne Hears the Warning

planSpec.audience: partners defending a romance from every caution
planSpec.stakes: let serious facts enter before commitments harden
planSpec.requiredBeat: a mother's warning about five years in psychiatric care breaks through infatuation

examples.scenario: Etienne finds his mother's note beside the wedding deposit envelope at the kitchen table: "Ask about the five years in psychiatric care." He wants to defend Bonnie before reading the rest. Before lunch, he must answer with more than loyalty, because love that cannot examine a serious fact is still being carried by the fantasy.
examples.whatToDo: Etienne thanks his mother for naming the fact, then schedules a calm conversation with Bonnie before another deposit turns speed into pressure.
examples.whyItMatters: The warning is not a verdict on Bonnie. It teaches that euphoria can treat sober information as betrayal exactly when open-eyed care is needed.

examples.title: Rocco Marks the Two-Year Drop

planSpec.audience: spouses afraid the missing rush means failure
planSpec.stakes: replace panic with chosen care after the high fades
planSpec.requiredBeat: two-year romantic obsession fading becomes a transition

examples.scenario: Rocco sorts anniversary cards on the apartment floor two years after the wedding. The old romantic obsession is gone, and Dorothy Tennov's word limerence is underlined in the class handout. Nothing blew up; breakfast simply feels ordinary. He circles the line that says a faded high can be a transition, not a verdict.
examples.whatToDo: Rocco names the drop without accusing Pascal, then chooses one steady act of care that does not depend on feeling swept away.
examples.whyItMatters: Two-year fading can scare a couple into false diagnosis. Naming the transition lets chosen behavior replace panic as the next evidence of love.

examples.title: Pascal Refills the Quiet Tank

planSpec.audience: spouses waiting for affection to feel automatic again
planSpec.stakes: meet emotional need after chemistry stops leading
planSpec.requiredBeat: real love chooses an act that fills the emotional tank

examples.scenario: Pascal crosses the word "fate" off a fridge note after a late shift. The apartment is quiet, Rocco is asleep, and the in-love obsession versus real love contrast from counseling sits on the counter. Before the morning routine swallows them, Pascal needs to choose a specific act that will help the emotional love tank feel full.
examples.whatToDo: Pascal leaves a concrete care note by the coffee mug and plans a short check-in, linking affection to a visible choice rather than to mood.
examples.whyItMatters: The love tank returns after the rush fades. Small chosen acts give security a place to land when chemistry is no longer doing the work.

examples.title: Bonnie Requests Open Eyes

planSpec.stakes: protect dignity by telling the truth before vows are planned
planSpec.requiredBeat: five years in psychiatric care must be known, not hidden by romance

examples.scenario: Bonnie folds the clinic form in the waiting room while Etienne rehearses cheerful promises. The form names five years of psychiatric care, the same fact his mother warned about. Before the counselor opens the door, Bonnie has to tell him that being loved well means being known clearly, not being idealized.
examples.whatToDo: Bonnie asks Etienne to discuss the history plainly with the counselor, then watches whether his care can stay present after the ideal image changes.
examples.whyItMatters: Open-eyed love protects dignity better than denial. A person is not served by being turned into a fantasy that cannot hold the truth.

questions.prompt: Jaspreet tells a class that Dorothy Tennov's limerence research gives romantic obsession an average span of about two years. Which reading best uses that fact?
choices: Jaspreet should treat the two-year mark as a reason to doubt every couple's sincerity.
Jaspreet should prepare couples for a normal fading of intensity rather than a failed marriage.
Jaspreet should advise couples to preserve the early rush by avoiding ordinary routines.
questions.explanation: The time span normalizes the fading of obsession. It does not mock the feeling or make marriage hopeless; it points couples toward chosen love after the high falls.

questions.prompt: Valerie announces an engagement after three weeks with Christophe, after years of relationships that did not last. What caution fits the source scene?
choices: Valerie's certainty may be running ahead of evidence, so she should slow down and learn more.
Valerie's years of disappointment mean the engagement should be treated as compensation.
Valerie's short timeline proves Christophe has solved the old pattern by creating a stronger feeling.
questions.explanation: The three-week engagement shows how euphoria can feel like settled knowledge. The issue is not the absence of feeling; it is certainty without enough lived evidence.

questions.prompt: When Etienne's mother raises Bonnie's five years in psychiatric care, Etienne calls the warning unloving. Which answer best preserves the hard edge?
choices: Etienne should dismiss the warning so his loyalty to Bonnie stays visible.
Etienne should let the warning define Bonnie before any further conversation.
Etienne should ask sober questions while still treating Bonnie as worthy of love.
questions.explanation: The warning scene is about narrowed judgment, not contempt. Mature care can hold dignity and serious facts together, while infatuation tends to filter facts out.

questions.prompt: Rocco says the old rush is gone, so the marriage has only two futures: endure a cold home or leave for another romance. Which response fits mature love?
choices: Rocco should wait for the rush to return before he changes any daily behavior.
Rocco should keep the cold home stable while expecting Pascal to need less affection.
Rocco should name a third path of deliberate care after the automatic high has faded.
questions.explanation: The argument rejects the misery-or-divorce frame. The fading of euphoria opens the need for chosen love rather than another hunt for intensity.

questions.prompt: Pascal worries that planned acts of love are less authentic than spontaneous affection. Which answer best reflects real love here?
choices: Pascal should rely on spontaneous warmth so the marriage does not feel managed.
Pascal can treat discipline as the structure that carries care when instinct no longer does.
Pascal should measure love by how little effort the next kind act requires.
questions.explanation: Choice and discipline do not cheapen love in this frame. They let care continue after the early state stops supplying effort without thought.

questions.prompt: Christophe says the emotional love tank mattered during dating but should not need attention now. What correction follows from the idea?
choices: Christophe should expect the love tank to need care again once romantic euphoria fades.
Christophe should assume the dating thrill has permanently solved the need for affection.
Christophe should discuss the tank only if the marriage began without romantic feeling.
questions.explanation: The in-love state can temporarily fill the emotional need. When it subsides, the need returns and has to be met through chosen behavior.

questions.prompt: Bonnie feels safer when Etienne loves with open eyes, and she has more energy for work and repair. What does that show about a full tank?
choices: Bonnie's security can free energy for growth instead of constant self-protection.
Bonnie's comfort should replace hard conversations so growth feels less risky.
Bonnie's next step should be proving she deserves the care before using it.
questions.explanation: Security is not mere comfort. A full emotional tank gives a spouse enough safety to move toward potential rather than spend energy defending worth.

questions.prompt: Which use of the five languages fits Jaspreet's lesson after the romantic high fades?
choices: Use them mainly during the dating thrill, while affection still feels easy.
Use them as labels for personality types, then stop adjusting daily behavior.
Use them as practical ways to meet emotional need when instinct stops supplying effort.
questions.explanation: The languages are tools for post-euphoria love. Their value is practical translation: they help a spouse give care in a form the other person receives.

questions.prompt: At breakfast, Valerie feels less dazzled by Christophe than she did at the start. Which conclusion avoids using the high as the maintenance standard?
choices: Valerie should read the drop as evidence that the first attraction was meaningless.
Valerie should expect the drop and begin measuring love by repeated chosen care.
Valerie should chase more intensity before ordinary perception settles into habit.
questions.explanation: A decline in euphoria is expected. The mature standard is not preserving the first high, but choosing love once ordinary perception returns.

reviewCards.front: What does the two-year limerence frame protect couples from misreading?
reviewCards.back: Dorothy Tennov's average span helps couples see fading romantic obsession as expected. The drop is not proof that love was false or that marriage has failed.

reviewCards.front: Why is the three-week engagement a caution rather than a model?
reviewCards.back: It shows how euphoria can create confidence before knowledge. A short timeline may feel clear because virtues glow and warnings shrink.

reviewCards.front: How can falling in love impair judgment?
reviewCards.back: The in-love state filters perception. Etienne can hear his mother's serious warning as disloyalty because attraction makes hard facts feel like threats.

reviewCards.front: What third path appears after the romantic high fades?
reviewCards.back: The couple is not limited to misery or leaving. They can build mature love through reason, choice, discipline, and care that meets emotional need.

reviewCards.front: Why does discipline belong inside real love?
reviewCards.back: Discipline gives love a practiced form after instinctive attraction stops carrying behavior. Chosen action can be more faithful than waiting for mood.

reviewCards.front: When do the five languages become especially practical?
reviewCards.back: They matter after euphoria fades, when spouses need reliable ways to fill the emotional tank instead of depending on the dating thrill.

implementationPlan.title: Run the Open-Eyes Love Check
implementationPlan.coreSkill: Practice separating the feeling of love from the choice to love. Run the Open-Eyes Love Check by naming the current romantic signal, the fact you may be avoiding, and one act of care you can choose with clear sight. The goal is not colder love; it is love that can survive ordinary sight.

ifThenPlans.context: If a new romance feels settled before you have seen stress, conflict, or routine
ifThenPlans.plan: If speed is doing the persuading, then run the Open-Eyes Love Check and write three facts you still need to learn before making a promise.

ifThenPlans.context: If a loved one raises a warning sign and your first impulse is to defend the romance
ifThenPlans.plan: If loyalty feels like refusing the warning, then run the Open-Eyes Love Check and discuss the fact without turning it into a verdict.

ifThenPlans.context: If the early rush has faded and the next thought is misery or escape
ifThenPlans.plan: If the high is gone, then run the Open-Eyes Love Check and choose one concrete act that fills the emotional tank today.

ifThenPlans.context: If a planned act of love feels less genuine than a spontaneous one
ifThenPlans.plan: If effort makes the act feel false, then run the Open-Eyes Love Check and name how discipline can serve the spouse's good.

implementationPlan.twentyFourHourChallenge: Within 24 hours, run the Open-Eyes Love Check once: name one feeling, one fact, and one chosen act of care. Put the act where your spouse will notice it.
implementationPlan.weeklyPractice: For seven days, repeat the Open-Eyes Love Check each evening. Track whether your chosen acts are based on clear knowledge or on chasing the old rush.
